findings.title: Certain temporal condition
findings.claim: إِذَا frames the promise's arrival as the time condition: the clause is heard as when that event comes, while its exact scope remains open.
findings.mechanism: The temporal particle opens a future protasis and the following arrival clause supplies its event; their contact makes the future grammatically expected rather than hypothetical.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the promise as an anticipated event that organizes the clause which follows.
findings.containment: This fixes the temporal force of the condition, not the promise's date, identity, or whether ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ means the latter promise or the Hereafter.

epistemic.reason: The particle, clause order, and candidate evidence are locally aligned and trusted.

findings.title: Promise arrival turns into bringing
findings.claim: The promise first arrives as the subject of جَآءَ, then the repeated coming root in جِئْنَا بِكُمْ carries the condition into divine bringing.
findings.mechanism: The first verb's arriving event meets the second verb's bāʾ-governed group complement; repetition links the clauses while the changed construction turns arrival into an act directed toward the addressees.
findings.reader_payoff: The condition and answer become a connected motion: an event arrives, and the addressed group is then brought.
findings.containment: Only the focus-local root repetition and construction are retained; the claimed returns from 17:5 and 17:7 are not used, and no destination or date is named.

epistemic.reason: Both word-analysis records and the focus alignment support the local repeated-root relation.

findings.title: The promise as arriving event
findings.claim: وَعْدُ is the nominative subject of جَآءَ, so the promise itself enters the clause as the event that arrives.
findings.mechanism: The intransitive arrival verb takes the construct promise as its subject; the genitive ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ specifies that promise rather than becoming a second subject.
findings.reader_payoff: An abstract undertaking becomes an event with a place in the conditional sequence, not only a statement previously spoken.
findings.containment: The local subject relation is clear; the earlier Surah 17 promise formulas at 17:5 and 17:7 are not part of this finding.

epistemic.reason: The attachment claim and local word alignment identify the nominative subject and genitive complement.

findings.title: Promise defined by its genitive
findings.claim: The construct head وَعْدُ is the arriving subject, and its genitive complement gives that event a latter or final horizon.
findings.mechanism: The noun's nominative relation to جَآءَ makes it the subject-event; its construct relation to ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ simultaneously narrows what promise arrives.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the event and its defining horizon held in one grammatical phrase.
findings.containment: The construction supports a latter/final complement, while the sequence through 17:5 and 17:7 is not used to define it.

epistemic.reason: The focus grammar independently supplies both the subject and construct relations.

findings.title: Promise and appointed time
findings.claim: وَعْدُ carries a future undertaking, and the إِذَا condition lets that promised event function as an appointment-like temporal trigger.
findings.mechanism: The promise noun meets the certain when-condition and the arrival verb; the contact turns a vague future reference into an event expected at its appointed occurrence.
findings.reader_payoff: Assurance and temporal expectation stay together in the promise phrase.
findings.containment: The focus gives no clock date or place. A threat remains within the root's broader range, but no harm or hostile outcome activates that reading here; 17:5 and 17:7 are not used.

epistemic.reason: The local conditional is clear, while the appointment branch's lexicon identity is qualified and the threat alternative lacks a focus trigger.
